new_statements.relation_note: Catalog record (Muraoka & Porten 1998/2003) is 'undetermined': no stress section, only incidental remarks that the 'traditional position of the stress' in *qatl > /'alep/-type nouns is penultimate and that penult stress of kl' cannot be decided. Segert is compatible and adds the general statement: traditional (Tiberian BA) main stress is word-final by default, penultimate only in listed classes (his 3.5.3.1 segolate class is exactly Muraoka-Porten's /'alep/ case), and Proto-Aramaic stress was penultimate, later shifted to the ultima by apocope/contraction/anaptyxis/analogy. He also states outright (3.5.1) that the unvocalised Old/Imperial Aramaic texts themselves yield only 'einige Indizien…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Segert treats all Old Aramaic (inscriptions, Imperial/Egyptian Aramaic papyri, Biblical Aramaic) in one grammar. Synchronic rule, taken from the Tiberian (and Babylonian) vocalisation of Biblical Aramaic because the consonantal Imperial-Aramaic texts themselves give only indirect clues: main stress falls on the final syllable of the word; penultimate stress is restricted to listed classes: 3.5.3.1 words/forms with an anaptyctic vowel (segolates, mélek < *malk-), 3.5.3.2-3.5.3.3 [not retrieved in the snippets], 3.5.3.4 forms whose penult was long and whose ultima was short and closed, where stress stayed in its original place. Diachronic rule: Proto-Aramaic stress was penultimate and strong (it drove vowel reduction/elision and the loss of short final vowels, §3.5.5, §3.9.4.1); it came to stand on the ultima through apocope of final short vowels (3.5.4.1, *hukmatu > hukmat type), contraction (3.5.4.2 hewō < *hawaju), anaptyxis/metathesis (3.5.4.3 šim'et < *šami'-et), and analogical shift (3.5.4.5 'emár < *'ámar 'say!', analogical to pl. 'emárū), with 'anā 'I' < *'ánā as a non-analogical shift (3.5.4.6). In Segert's transcription an acute marks penult main stress; all unmarked words are final-stressed (§2.5.5.2).
new_statements.secondary_stress: §2.5.5.3 'Der Nebenton': secondary stress is noted in the Tiberian text by meteg (the small vertical stroke under the letter); Segert describes only the notation, no placement rule is visible in the fragments.
new_statements.exceptions: Penult-stressed classes 3.5.3.1 (segolates / anaptyctic-vowel forms) and 3.5.3.4 (long penult + short closed ultima keeps original stress); 3.5.3.2-3.5.3.3 exist but their content was not retrieved; 'anā 'I' cited as an irregular (non-analogical) shift to the ultima; the whole rule is explicitly conditioned on the reliability of the Masoretic tradition (3.5.1: 'deren Realität aber von der Verläßlichkeit der [..] überhaupt abhängt').
new_statements.identity_note: Segert's grammar covers 'alle altaramäischen Texte vom Anfang bis etwa zum Beginn der christlichen Ära' (Old Aramaic inscriptions, Imperial/Egyptian Aramaic papyri and ostraca, Biblical Aramaic), excluding Nabataean and Palmyrene; the stress rule in §3.5.2-3.5.3 is explicitly that of the Tiberian (and Babylonian) vocalisation of Biblical Aramaic, applied to Altaramäisch as a whole; §3.5.4-3.5.5 are reconstruction (Proto-Aramaic penult stress). impe1235 (Imperial Aramaic, 5th c. BCE Egypt) is inside the grammar's scope but has no vocalised texts of its own.
